newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- FEB 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- FEB 12.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The government is attempting to introduce a new wages and incentives system based on productivity and granting performance-related bonuses, free shares, low interest loans, extra leave and increased social security benefits in the wider public sector, beginning with profit-making state enterprises, such as Greece's telecoms organisation, OTE.

--The apparently worsening situation in neighbouring Albania has fuelled fears in Athens of a new wave of illegal immigrants through the Greek-Albanian border. The foreign ministry revealed yesterday that Athens would launch an initiative through the European Union that would forward financial aid to Balkan countries in an effort to restore stability in the region.

--Prime Minister Costas Simitis emphasised ruling party PASOK's social profile and the need for dialogue as he announced works totalling 40 billion drachmas for western Attica last night. Simitis made clear that the government would not change its economic policy or bow to demands.

--Various sectors of the civil service have begun labour action, signalling a new wave of strikes for the country. Civil servants are reacting against the government's decision to cut back on a number of allowances and bonuses.

--Albania and the Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia have requested access to the northern Greek Egnatia road axis. Bulgaria and Turkey have also expressed strong interest. Meanwhile, a recent Community study has called the proposal to build a parallel Balkans highway, shadowing the route of the Egnatia, "unfeasible".

--Simitis was adamant last night that the government would not bow to "blackmail by unions", saying succumbing to demands and hand-outs would lead the country to "Albanisation" and debt, with workers the first to pay.

--The government appealed to teachers yesterday to return to their classrooms, saying there were no margins for further increases. High school teachers however appear determined to continue their strike for a fifth week, while primary school teachers are undecided. A decision is expected today.
--The Athens bourse reached a new record yesterday, with the general price index reaching a high of 1,263 points before closing at 1,244, up 1.96 percent.
--A roundtable discussion between teachers and government has shown that there appears to be little chance of finding a way out of the impasse.
--A fan of television personality Eleni Menegaki was yesterday sentenced to 11 months jail after he threatened two security guards with a rifle to let him through to see his idol. ELEFTHEROS TYPOS

--Agriculture Minister Stephanos Tzoumakas has said he will bring up the issue of his supposed siesta at a Council of Agriculture Ministers luncheon, reported in the "European Voice" newspaper, reports say.
--Greeks are not the lovers they thought they were, according to a recent study. One in four women are dissatisfied by their love lives while eight in ten have never had an orgasm.
--Turkish fans chanted "war, war" during a basketball match between Apollon Patron and RTT Ankara yesterday.

--Students have thrown their glove into the ring, saying they will occupy schools if the school year is extended to make up for lessons lost over the past four weeks of the teachers' strike. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
